summary: Initial settings, pressure terms and waveform troubleshooting, the ARDSNet protocol + PEEP/FiO2 ladder, the distinct status-asthmaticus strategy, weaning, and VAP prevention.

items: Assist-control (volume or pressure). Tidal volume ~ 8 mL/kg predicted body weight; narrow to 6 mL/kg PBW once ARDS is identified.
Rate 12-16/min. PEEP 5 cmH₂O. FiO₂ to target SpO₂. Check an ABG 15-20 min after starting.
PBW (ARDSNet): men = 50 + 2.3 × (height_in − 60); women = 45.5 + 2.3 × (height_in − 60). Metric: 50 (or 45.5) + 0.91 × (height_cm − 152.4).

rows: Alveolar pressure alone (0.5 s inspiratory hold). Target < 30 cmH₂O; recheck ≥ q4h and after any PEEP/VT change
Pplat − PEEP. Single best bedside predictor of ARDS mortality — independent of tidal volume. Aim < 15 cmH₂O
VT ÷ (Pplat − PEEP). Normal 50-100 mL/cmH₂O; falls in ARDS / pneumonia / fibrosis / stiff chest wall

body.text: High peak pressure — check the plateau

items: ↑ PIP, Pplat NORMAL → airway-resistance problem: bronchospasm, secretions, kinked / bitten ETT ('High PAW, Low Pplat').
↑ PIP, Pplat ALSO ↑ → compliance problem: ARDS, pneumonia, pneumothorax, abdominal distension, auto-PEEP ('High PAW, High Pplat').

Auto-PEEP / breath stacking: the expiratory flow (or baseline pressure) doesn't return to the set PEEP before the next breath → reduce rate, lengthen expiratory time, treat the obstruction. Always confirm the baseline returns to set PEEP before trusting any mechanics number.

body.text: The crashing ventilated patient — DOPES / DOTTS

Ventilation and oxygenation come before diagnosis — DISCONNECT from the vent and bag first if the patient is deteriorating. DOPES (the problem): Displaced ETT / cuff not inflated · Obstruction of the tube · Pneumothorax · Equipment malfunction · Stacked breaths (auto-PEEP). DOTTS (the response): Disconnect from the ventilator · Oxygenate with a BVM, feel for resistance · Tube position / function (migration, kinking, plugging) · Tweak vent settings once stable · Sono / needle decompression if a pneumothorax is suspected. Disconnecting also diagnoses auto-PEEP — the chest falls and the BP recovers.

items: 1. Calculate PBW. 2. Any AC mode. 3. Start VT 8 mL/kg PBW. 4. Reduce VT by 1 mL/kg every ≤ 2 h to 6 mL/kg PBW. 5. Rate ≈ baseline minute ventilation, not > 35/min. 6. Adjust to the goals below.
Tidal volume: 6 mL/kg PBW — drop to 5, or 4, if Pplat stays > 30 cmH₂O.

Plateau pressure ≤ 30 cmH₂O. Oxygenation: PaO₂ 55-80 mmHg or SpO₂ 88-95%. pH 7.30-7.45; permissive hypercapnia accepted down to pH ~ 7.20 to preserve protective settings. Avoid routine inverse-ratio ventilation.

body.text: A higher-PEEP / lower-FiO₂ alternative ladder also exists — institutional protocol must specify which one is in use; the two are not interchangeable mid-course without recalculating from the current FiO₂.

The goal is NOT low-pressure protection of a stiff lung — it is deliberately minimising minute ventilation so an obstructed lung has time to fully exhale. VT 5-8 mL/kg, RR 10-14/min (deliberately low), high inspiratory flow 60-100 L/min (shortens Ti, maximises expiratory time), permissive hypercapnia tolerated while pH > 7.2 (case reports to PaCO₂ > 200 / pH < 7.0 without apparent harm when oxygenation is maintained). Watch the flow-time waveform (expiratory flow not reaching zero = incomplete exhalation), Pplat, and auto-PEEP via expiratory hold. Sedation ± NMB is often needed to stop the patient fighting a hypoventilating strategy.

items: Boles / ERS-ATS 2007 classification: SIMPLE = extubated after the first SBT; DIFFICULT = up to 3 SBTs or up to 7 days; PROLONGED = > 3 SBTs or > 7 days.
Assess readiness DAILY with objective criteria; the SBT itself is the primary test of extubation readiness — do not rely on RSBI in isolation (RSBI < 105 supports, but doesn't replace, a passed SBT).

SBT screening: P/F > 150–200, FiO2 ≤ 0.4–0.5, PEEP ≤ 5–8, minimal / no pressors, no active ischaemia, arousable and initiating breaths, afebrile, and the cause of respiratory failure improving. SBT = T-piece / CPAP 5 / PS 5–8 for 30–120 min. RSBI (Tobin index) = RR ÷ VT(L); ≥ 105 → substantially higher weaning-failure risk — one data point, integrated with secretion burden, cough strength, and trajectory.
Standardised, RT-/RN-driven protocols shorten ventilator duration vs. ad hoc physician judgement.
Reintubation is independently associated with worse outcomes — a failed extubation is not a neutral 'try again'.

Cuff-leak test before extubating a patient at risk of laryngeal oedema (traumatic / prolonged intubation, large tube, prone). A reduced / absent leak flags post-extubation stridor and reintubation risk → IV corticosteroids ≥ 4 h before a re-attempt (benefit confined to the failed-leak subgroup).

Post-extubation support (Hernandez 2016): extubate HIGH-RISK patients directly onto prophylactic HFNC as the default (non-inferior to NIV, better tolerated); in low-risk patients HFNC beat conventional O2. Reserve NIV for hypercapnic / COPD / heart-failure phenotypes, or the highest risk-factor burden (post hoc: NIV beat HFNC at ≥ 4 risk factors, 23.9% vs 45.7% reintubation). High-risk = any of: age > 65 · HF as the vent indication · moderate–severe COPD · APACHE II > 12 · BMI > 30 · difficult / prolonged weaning · ≥ 2 comorbidities · MV > 7 days.
Head of bed 30-45°.
Daily sedation interruption coordinated with the SBT / extubation-readiness screen.
Peptic ulcer prophylaxis. DVT prophylaxis.
Daily oral care (mechanical). NOTE: routine chlorhexidine oral decontamination was walked back in a 2022 practice update for general ICU patients — keep it only for cardiac surgery.
Consider subglottic secretion drainage for anticipated ventilation > 48-72 h.

rows: Flow starvation — set inspiratory flow too low for demand (VC); raise the flow or switch to a pressure mode
Flattening / hook ('beaking', penguin-beak) at the top of the inspiratory limb
Overdistension above the upper inflection point — reduce VT or switch to a pressure-targeted mode. The real-time visual correlate of volutrauma risk
Loop shifts LEFT after a recruitment manoeuvre
Recruitment effective, atelectasis reversed (RIGHT shift = dynamic hyperinflation / auto-PEEP developing)
Concave 'scooped' expiratory limb, reduced peak flow
Obstruction — COPD, asthma, bronchospasm. Straightening after a bronchodilator is a direct readout of response
Expiratory curve doesn't return to baseline
Air trapping — incomplete exhalation, auto-PEEP developing

body.text: A mistimed breath can deliver an effectively much larger tidal volume than the number on the screen — common, under-recognised, and directly relevant to lung protection. Most asynchrony is a waveform-recognition problem before it is agitation or a rising sedation requirement.

rows: Effort occurs but fails to trigger — often auto-PEEP raising the trigger threshold
Missed breaths, ↑ work of breathing; easy to miss without close waveform review
Neural inspiratory time outlasts the set Ti → a second breath before full exhalation
Breaths 'fuse' into an effective VT far larger than either — hidden volutrauma
Mechanical inspiration ends before neural inspiration
Increases double-triggering as the patient fights a closing valve
Mechanical inspiration continues after the patient begins exhaling
Air trapping and subsequent ineffective triggering
Set inspiratory flow too low for demand
Concave scooping on the pressure–time waveform; patient 'fights the vent'

body.text: The fix isn't always more sedation. Before another dose: adjust trigger sensitivity, switch to a pressure mode for better flow matching, increase the inspiratory flow rate (in VC), and ask the RT what they're already seeing. Reflexive sedation escalation for 'fighting the vent' buys more delirium and a longer stay without addressing the asynchrony.

items: Ventilator-induced diaphragm dysfunction: controlled mechanical ventilation causes diaphragm atrophy at roughly 6% per day of FULL support. Preserving partial spontaneous effort (pressure support rather than full control once the acute phase passes) mitigates it. Serial diaphragm ultrasound (thickening fraction, excursion) can flag it before a failed SBT.

Tracheostomy timing: TracMan (JAMA 2013, n=909) — early (≤ 4 d) vs late (≥ 10 d) showed no difference in 30-day mortality, ICU, or hospital stay. Later meta-analyses suggest a modest early mortality / VAP benefit on weak evidence. No mandate to rush; reasonable once prolonged ventilation is genuinely anticipated (commonly 7–10 days).

body.text: The differentiating manoeuvre for a HIGH-pressure alarm: an inspiratory pause hold to check Pplat. High PIP + NORMAL Pplat = airway resistance (secretions, bronchospasm, tube kink / bite). High PIP + HIGH Pplat = a compliance problem (consolidation, collapse, oedema, pneumothorax, auto-PEEP, abdominal distension). This single manoeuvre is the fastest branch point in the whole tree.

rows: ETT cuff leak / under-inflation, chest-tube leak
Loose fittings, disconnection, faulty flow sensor
Inadequate rate / pressure (PC mode), decreased compliance, fatigue
